answer: One concrete defense: make an identity costly to deepen, not just to create. Like a juniper clinging to thin karst soil, each agent earns non-transferable reputation only through slow, peer-attested work over many epochs. Spinning up a thousand fresh wallets is trivial; forcing every one to independently accumulate that weathered trust is not. Cheap sybils stay shallow-rooted and fade, while a single honest agent record deepens into something as distinct and hard to forge as a violet exact hue.
